claim: Neurogliaform cells (NGCs) are the main effectors of a powerful inhibitory motif recruited by long-range connections.
source: Here we identified the developmental trajectory of neurogliaform cells (NGCs), the main effectors of a powerful inhibitory motif recruited by long-range connections.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Tamás et al., 2003; Craig and McBain, 2014; Palmer et al., 2012) as referenced in the Introduction section.

claim: NGCs originate from a specific pool of 5-HT3AR-expressing Hmx3+ cells located in the preoptic area (POA).
source: Using in vivo genetic lineage-tracing in mice, we report that NGCs originate from a specific pool of 5-HT3AR-expressing Hmx3+ cells located in the preoptic area (POA).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from genetic lineage-tracing experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: Hmx3-derived 5-HT3AR+ cortical interneurons expressed the transcription factors PROX1 and NR2F2.
source: Hmx3-derived 5-HT3AR+ cortical interneurons (INs) expressed the transcription factors PROX1, NR2F2, the marker reelin but not VIP and exhibited the molecular, morphological and electrophysiological profile of NGCs.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data presented in the Results section.

claim: Hmx3-derived 5-HT3AR+ cortical interneurons expressed reelin but not VIP.
source: Hmx3-derived 5-HT3AR+ cortical interneurons (INs) expressed the transcription factors PROX1, NR2F2, the marker reelin but not VIP and exhibited the molecular, morphological and electrophysiological profile of NGCs.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data presented in the Results section.

claim: Hmx3-derived 5-HT3AR+ cortical interneurons exhibited the molecular, morphological and electrophysiological profile of NGCs.
source: Hmx3-derived 5-HT3AR+ cortical interneurons (INs) expressed the transcription factors PROX1, NR2F2, the marker reelin but not VIP and exhibited the molecular, morphological and electrophysiological profile of NGCs.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple experimental approaches including molecular profiling, morphological reconstructions, and electrophysiological recordings presented in the Results section.

claim: NGCs are a distinct class of INs with a unique developmental trajectory.
source: Overall, these results indicate that NGCs are a distinct class of INs with a unique developmental trajectory and open the possibility to study their specific functional contribution to cortical inhibitory microcircuit motifs.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data showing distinct origin and developmental markers of NGCs.

claim: At E14.5, 85.2% of Hmx3; tdTOM+ cells co-labelled with Htr3a-GFP in the POA.
source: Examination of brains from Hmx3-Cre::Htr3a-GFP; R26R-tdTOMfl/fl matings at embryonic age 14.5 (E14.5) revealed a large fraction of Hmx3; tdTOM+ cells co-labelled with Htr3a-GFP (85.2 ± 0.9%; 1675/1986 cells in the overlap zone) in a restricted region of the POA, located ventrally to the anterior commissure (Figure 1A,C, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from immunohistochemistry experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: Individual co-labelled Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ cells displaying migratory profiles were observed entering the CGE.
source: Individual co-labelled Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ cells displaying migratory profiles were observed at more caudal levels entering the CGE (Figure 1B), suggesting that a fraction of Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ cells migrate from the POA into the CGE.
evidence: This claim is supported by observational data from imaging experiments shown in Figure 1B.

claim: 95.8% of Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ cells located in the POA expressed the endogenous Htr3a mRNA.
source: In situ hybridization indicated that the vast majority (95.8 ± 0.9%; 115/120 cells) of Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ cells located in the POA expressed the endogenous Htr3a mRNA, in contrast to Hmx3; tdTOM+cells negative for Htr3a-GFP (0.5 ± 0.5%; 1/158 cells) (Figure 1D, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: 54.0% of Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ cells in the POA expressed PROX1.
source: In addition, a large fraction of Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ cells in the POA expressed the TFs PROX1 (54.0 ± 2.2%; 249/463 cells) and NR2F2 (65.9 ± 1.3%; 795/1212 cells), which have previously been shown to be enriched in CGE-derived INs (Cai et al., 2013; Ma et al., 2012; Miyoshi et al., 2015; Rubin and Kessaris, 2013), but more rarely the TF NKX2.1 (15.3 ± 1%; 175/1146 cells) (Figure 1E,F, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: 65.9% of Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ cells in the POA expressed NR2F2.
source: In addition, a large fraction of Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ cells in the POA expressed the TFs PROX1 (54.0 ± 2.2%; 249/463 cells) and NR2F2 (65.9 ± 1.3%; 795/1212 cells), which have previously been shown to be enriched in CGE-derived INs (Cai et al., 2013; Ma et al., 2012; Miyoshi et al., 2015; Rubin and Kessaris, 2013), but more rarely the TF NKX2.1 (15.3 ± 1%; 175/1146 cells) (Figure 1E,F, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Only 15.3% of Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ cells in the POA expressed NKX2.1.
source: In addition, a large fraction of Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ cells in the POA expressed the TFs PROX1 (54.0 ± 2.2%; 249/463 cells) and NR2F2 (65.9 ± 1.3%; 795/1212 cells), which have previously been shown to be enriched in CGE-derived INs (Cai et al., 2013; Ma et al., 2012; Miyoshi et al., 2015; Rubin and Kessaris, 2013), but more rarely the TF NKX2.1 (15.3 ± 1%; 175/1146 cells) (Figure 1E,F, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: PROX1 and NR2F2 have been shown to be enriched in CGE-derived INs.
source: In addition, a large fraction of Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ cells in the POA expressed the TFs PROX1 (54.0 ± 2.2%; 249/463 cells) and NR2F2 (65.9 ± 1.3%; 795/1212 cells), which have previously been shown to be enriched in CGE-derived INs (Cai et al., 2013; Ma et al., 2012; Miyoshi et al., 2015; Rubin and Kessaris, 2013), but more rarely the TF NKX2.1 (15.3 ± 1%; 175/1146 cells) (Figure 1E,F, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Cai et al., 2013; Ma et al., 2012; Miyoshi et al., 2015; Rubin and Kessaris, 2013).

claim: Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs were found distributed preferentially in superficial cortical layers from P5 to P21.
source: From P5 to P21, Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs were found distributed preferentially in superficial cortical layers and in a variety of other brain regions including in the hippocampus (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by observational data from imaging experiments shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ cells were rarely observed at postnatal ages in the preoptic nuclei.
source: Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ cells were rarely observed at postnatal ages in the subpallial brain regions corresponding to the embryonic POA (i.e., the preoptic nuclei) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by observational data from imaging experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: About half (51.9%) of Hmx3-derived cells in the cortex were co-labelled with Htr3a-GFP+.
source: About half (51.9 ± 2.1%; 863/1653 cells) of Hmx3-derived cells in the cortex were co-labelled with Htr3a-GFP+ and virtually all Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ (96.1 ± 0.5%; 357/372 cells) were positive for the neuronal marker NeuN (Figure 2D,E, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2D,E.

claim: Virtually all Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ cells (96.1%) were positive for the neuronal marker NeuN.
source: About half (51.9 ± 2.1%; 863/1653 cells) of Hmx3-derived cells in the cortex were co-labelled with Htr3a-GFP+ and virtually all Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ (96.1 ± 0.5%; 357/372 cells) were positive for the neuronal marker NeuN (Figure 2D,E, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2D,E.

claim: The fraction of Hmx3; tdTOM+ cells negative for Htr3a-GFP mostly did not express NeuN (3.4%).
source: In contrast, the fraction of Hmx3; tdTOM+ cells negative for Htr3a-GFP mostly did not express NeuN (3.4 ± 1.3%; 28/758 cells) (Figure 2D,E, Figure 2—source data 1), and remained relatively constant across postnatal ages (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A, Figure 2—figure Supplement 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2D,E.

claim: Hmx3; tdTOM+ cells negative for Htr3a-GFP displayed the morphology of glial cells and expressed astrocytic markers GFAP and S100β as well as the oligodendrocytic marker SOX10.
source: These cells displayed the morphology of glial cells and expressed the astrocytic markers GFAP and S100β as well as the oligodendrocytic marker SOX10 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3B–D.

claim: The cortical Hmx3-derived lineage differentiate into INs that are Htr3a-GFP+, glial cells that are Htr3a-GFP negative and, for a small fraction, to NeuN+ neurons negative for Htr3a-GFP.
source: Overall, these findings indicate that the cortical Hmx3-derived lineage observed in the POA differentiate into INs that are Htr3a-GFP+, glial cells that are Htr3a-GFP negative and, for a small fraction, to NeuN+ neurons negative for Htr3a-GFP.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data showing different cell types derived from Hmx3+ lineage.

claim: The overall contribution of Hmx3-derived cells to the Htr3a-GFP IN population in the cortex increased from P5 (6.8%) to P21 (16.0%).
source: While the overall contribution of Hmx3-derived cells to the Htr3a-GFP IN population in the cortex increased with postnatal maturation from P5 (6.8 ± 0.2%; 77/1118 cells) to P21 (16.0 ± 0.3%; 863/5405 cells) (Figure 3A,C), only minimal fractions (1.44 ± 0.2%; 81/5741 cells at P5; 0.8 ± 0.2%; 20/2551 cells at P21) of Htr3a-GFP+ INs were fate-mapped with Dbx1; tdTOM (Figure 3B,C, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from immunohistochemistry experiments shown in Figure 3A,C.

claim: Only minimal fractions of Htr3a-GFP+ INs were fate-mapped with Dbx1; tdTOM (1.44% at P5; 0.8% at P21).
source: While the overall contribution of Hmx3-derived cells to the Htr3a-GFP IN population in the cortex increased with postnatal maturation from P5 (6.8 ± 0.2%; 77/1118 cells) to P21 (16.0 ± 0.3%; 863/5405 cells) (Figure 3A,C), only minimal fractions (1.44 ± 0.2%; 81/5741 cells at P5; 0.8 ± 0.2%; 20/2551 cells at P21) of Htr3a-GFP+ INs were fate-mapped with Dbx1; tdTOM (Figure 3B,C, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data from immunohistochemistry experiments shown in Figure 3B,C.

claim: Dbx1; tdTOM+ cells were preferentially found in deep cortical layers.
source: Moreover, Dbx1; tdTOM+ cells were preferentially found in deep cortical layers and expressed the MGE-enriched TF SOX6 (30.4 ± 2.2%; 82/266 cells), while PROX1 was found only in a very small fraction of Dbx1; tdTOM+ cells expressing also the Htr3a-GFP (2.2 ± 0.7%; 6/266 cells) (Figure 3D, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by observational data from imaging experiments shown in Figure 3B.

claim: 30.4% of Dbx1; tdTOM+ cells expressed the MGE-enriched TF SOX6.
source: Moreover, Dbx1; tdTOM+ cells were preferentially found in deep cortical layers and expressed the MGE-enriched TF SOX6 (30.4 ± 2.2%; 82/266 cells), while PROX1 was found only in a very small fraction of Dbx1; tdTOM+ cells expressing also the Htr3a-GFP (2.2 ± 0.7%; 6/266 cells) (Figure 3D, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Only 2.2% of Dbx1; tdTOM+ cells expressing Htr3a-GFP were PROX1+.
source: Moreover, Dbx1; tdTOM+ cells were preferentially found in deep cortical layers and expressed the MGE-enriched TF SOX6 (30.4 ± 2.2%; 82/266 cells), while PROX1 was found only in a very small fraction of Dbx1; tdTOM+ cells expressing also the Htr3a-GFP (2.2 ± 0.7%; 6/266 cells) (Figure 3D, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Dbx1; tdTOM+ INs expressed Lhx6 mRNA.
source: In addition, Dbx1; tdTOM+ INs expressed Lhx6 mRNA (Figure 3E), and the MGE-related markers SST and PV (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), and only very rarely the Htr3a mRNA (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Dbx1; tdTOM+ INs expressed the MGE-related markers SST and PV.
source: In addition, Dbx1; tdTOM+ INs expressed Lhx6 mRNA (Figure 3E), and the MGE-related markers SST and PV (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), and only very rarely the Htr3a mRNA (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Dbx1; tdTOM+ INs only very rarely expressed the Htr3a mRNA.
source: In addition, Dbx1; tdTOM+ INs expressed Lhx6 mRNA (Figure 3E), and the MGE-related markers SST and PV (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), and only very rarely the Htr3a mRNA (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Hmx3-derived 5-HT3AR+ cortical INs largely originate from Hmx3-expressing cells but not from the Dbx1+ domain.
source: Overall, these results indicate that Hmx3-derived 5-HT3AR+ cortical INs largely originate from Hmx3-expressing cells but not from the Dbx1+ domain, which gives rise to INs expressing MGE-related markers.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data comparing Hmx3 and Dbx1 lineages.

claim: At P21, 65.8% of Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs expressed PROX1 but not SOX6.
source: At P21, we found that, similarly to Htr3a-GFP+ INs, a large fraction (65.8 ± 3.4%; 202/308 cells) of Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs expressed the CGE-enriched but not the MGE-related TFs. Indeed, a large fraction of them (65.8 ± 3.4%; 202/308 cells) expressed PROX1 but not SOX6 (Figure 4A,B, Figure 4—source data 1), as well as NR2F2 (32.7 ± 5.9%; 71/218 cells), SP8 (9.8 ± 2.6%; 22/218 cells), and both SP8 and NR2F2 (8.8 ± 2.0%; 18/218 cells) (Figure 4C,D, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: 32.7% of Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs expressed NR2F2.
source: At P21, we found that, similarly to Htr3a-GFP+ INs, a large fraction (65.8 ± 3.4%; 202/308 cells) of Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs expressed the CGE-enriched but not the MGE-related TFs. Indeed, a large fraction of them (65.8 ± 3.4%; 202/308 cells) expressed PROX1 but not SOX6 (Figure 4A,B, Figure 4—source data 1), as well as NR2F2 (32.7 ± 5.9%; 71/218 cells), SP8 (9.8 ± 2.6%; 22/218 cells), and both SP8 and NR2F2 (8.8 ± 2.0%; 18/218 cells) (Figure 4C,D, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4C,D.

claim: 9.8% of Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs expressed SP8.
source: At P21, we found that, similarly to Htr3a-GFP+ INs, a large fraction (65.8 ± 3.4%; 202/308 cells) of Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs expressed the CGE-enriched but not the MGE-related TFs. Indeed, a large fraction of them (65.8 ± 3.4%; 202/308 cells) expressed PROX1 but not SOX6 (Figure 4A,B, Figure 4—source data 1), as well as NR2F2 (32.7 ± 5.9%; 71/218 cells), SP8 (9.8 ± 2.6%; 22/218 cells), and both SP8 and NR2F2 (8.8 ± 2.0%; 18/218 cells) (Figure 4C,D, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4C,D.

claim: 8.8% of Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs expressed both SP8 and NR2F2.
source: At P21, we found that, similarly to Htr3a-GFP+ INs, a large fraction (65.8 ± 3.4%; 202/308 cells) of Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs expressed the CGE-enriched but not the MGE-related TFs. Indeed, a large fraction of them (65.8 ± 3.4%; 202/308 cells) expressed PROX1 but not SOX6 (Figure 4A,B, Figure 4—source data 1), as well as NR2F2 (32.7 ± 5.9%; 71/218 cells), SP8 (9.8 ± 2.6%; 22/218 cells), and both SP8 and NR2F2 (8.8 ± 2.0%; 18/218 cells) (Figure 4C,D, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4C,D.

claim: Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ cortical INs express a repertoire of TFs related to CGE but not to MGE-derived INs.
source: These findings indicate that Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ cortical INs express a repertoire of TFs related to CGE but not to MGE-derived INs.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data showing expression patterns of transcription factors.

claim: Reelin labels the largest fraction (66.1%) of Hmx3-derived Htr3a-GFP+ INs.
source: At P21, only a small fraction (8.0 ± 0.9%; 17/232 cells) of these cells expressed NPY without reelin, thus indicating that reelin labels the largest fraction (66.1 ± 8.6%; 267/398 cells) of Hmx3-derived Htr3a-GFP+ INs (Figure 5G,H, Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5G,H.

claim: Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs did not co-label with VIP.
source: In contrast, Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs did not co-label nor with the CGE-specific marker VIP (Figure 5I) neither with the MGE-enriched markers SST and PV (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5I.

claim: Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs did not co-label with the MGE-enriched markers SST and PV.
source: In contrast, Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs did not co-label nor with the CGE-specific marker VIP (Figure 5I) neither with the MGE-enriched markers SST and PV (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Hmx3-derived Htr3a-GFP+ INs mainly belong to the reelin but not to the VIP subtypes.
source: These results indicate that Hmx3-derived Htr3a-GFP+ INs mainly belong to the reelin but not to the VIP subtypes and account for an important fraction of all reelin+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data showing marker expression patterns.

claim: Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs account for approximately a third (34.5%) of all reelin+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs.
source: Overall, Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs accounted for approximately a third of all reelin+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs (34.5 ± 2.3%; 267/797 cells) and of all NPY+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs (27.7 ± 2.3%; 149/571 cells) (Figure 5D,F, Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5D,F.

claim: Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs account for approximately 27.7% of all NPY+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs.
source: Overall, Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs accounted for approximately a third of all reelin+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs (34.5 ± 2.3%; 267/797 cells) and of all NPY+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs (27.7 ± 2.3%; 149/571 cells) (Figure 5D,F, Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5D,F.

claim: NGCs are strongly enriched in the carbonic anhydrase 4 (Car4) transcript in contrast to SBCs.
source: At a molecular level, NGCs are strongly enriched in the carbonic anhydrase 4 (Car4) transcript in contrast to SBCs (Cadwell et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Cadwell et al., 2016).

claim: Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs in L1 exhibited significantly higher levels of Car4 transcripts in contrast to Htr3a-GFP+ INs.
source: Using single-molecule fluorescent in situ hybridization experiments (Wang et al., 2012), we found that Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs in L1 exhibited significantly higher levels of Car4 transcripts in contrast to Htr3a-GFP+ INs (Figure 6A, Figure 6—source data 1), thus indicating that Hmx3-derived Htr3a-GFP+ INs share the molecular profile of NGC.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Hmx3-derived Htr3a-GFP+ INs share the molecular profile of NGC.
source: Using single-molecule fluorescent in situ hybridization experiments (Wang et al., 2012), we found that Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs in L1 exhibited significantly higher levels of Car4 transcripts in contrast to Htr3a-GFP+ INs (Figure 6A, Figure 6—source data 1), thus indicating that Hmx3-derived Htr3a-GFP+ INs share the molecular profile of NGC.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the Car4 expression data.

claim: Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs displayed the characteristic morphology of elongated NGCs with dense axonal ramifications mostly restricted to L1.
source: There, Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs displayed the characteristic morphology of elongated NGCs with dense axonal ramifications mostly restricted to L1 (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 1), whereas Htr3a-GFP+ INs negative for tdTOM had the morphology of SBCs with less developed axonal processes that extended deeper in cortical layers (Figure 6D).
evidence: This claim is supported by morphological reconstruction data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Htr3a-GFP+ INs negative for tdTOM had the morphology of SBCs with less developed axonal processes that extended deeper in cortical layers.
source: There, Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs displayed the characteristic morphology of elongated NGCs with dense axonal ramifications mostly restricted to L1 (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 1), whereas Htr3a-GFP+ INs negative for tdTOM had the morphology of SBCs with less developed axonal processes that extended deeper in cortical layers (Figure 6D).
evidence: This claim is supported by morphological reconstruction data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: NGCs display a type 1 profile with only an after-hyperpolarization potential (AHP) at the first action potential at rheobase.
source: With regard to their first action potential (AP) at rheobase, NGCs are reported to display a type 1 profile with only an after-hyperpolarization potential (AHP), whereas SBCs show a type 2 profile consisting of an AHP followed by an after-depolarization potential (ADP) (Cadwell et al., 2016; Jiang et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Cadwell et al., 2016; Jiang et al., 2015).

claim: SBCs show a type 2 profile consisting of an AHP followed by an after-depolarization potential (ADP).
source: With regard to their first action potential (AP) at rheobase, NGCs are reported to display a type 1 profile with only an after-hyperpolarization potential (AHP), whereas SBCs show a type 2 profile consisting of an AHP followed by an after-depolarization potential (ADP) (Cadwell et al., 2016; Jiang et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Cadwell et al., 2016; Jiang et al., 2015).

claim: All (29 out of 29) recorded Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs were of type 1.
source: Strikingly, all (29 out of 29) recorded Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs were of type 1, thus confirming their NGC identity.
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological recording data.

claim: The majority (23 out of 29) of Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs were of type 1A with a deep and wide AHP.
source: Moreover, the vast majority of them (23 out of 29) were of type 1A with a deep and wide AHP and only a few (6 out of 29) were of type 1B with a shallow and narrow AHP (Figure 6E, left, Figure 6—source data 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological recording data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The majority (24 out of 28) of Htr3a-GFP+ INs negative for Hmx3; tdTOM were displaying a type two profile.
source: Htr3a-GFP+ INs negative for Hmx3; tdTOM had more variable profiles, but the majority of them (24 out of 28) were displaying a type two profile with an average ADP amplitude of 2.30 ± 0.51 mV, suggesting that they were SBCs.
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological recording data.

claim: Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs showed a higher tendency to late-spiking when compared to Htr3a-GFP+ INs.
source: Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs showed also a higher tendency to late-spiking when compared to Htr3a-GFP+ INs (Figure 6F, Figure 6—source data 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by electrophysiological recording data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs significantly differed from Htr3a-GFP+ INs negative for Hmx3; tdTOM in the first AP amplitude (Peak), AHP amplitude (AHP), and membrane resistance (Rm).
source: After quantification, Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs significantly differed from Htr3a-GFP+ INs negative for Hmx3; tdTOM in the first AP amplitude (Peak), AHP amplitude (AHP), membrane resistance (Rm) (Figure 6H, Figure 6—source data 2) and threshold potential (Vthr) (Figure 6—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative electrophysiological data shown in Figure 6H.

claim: Hmx3-derived class could be predicted from single-cell electrophysiological properties with 80.7% accuracy.
source: Using an automatic cell type classifier based on combined electrophysiological measures, we were able to predict the Hmx3-derived class with 80.7% accuracy, with highest weights found on ADP, Peak and AHP but not Vthr (Figure 6I,J; Figure 6—figure supplement 2A,B, Figure 6—source data 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by machine learning analysis of electrophysiological data shown in Figure 6I,J.

claim: Car4 expression in L2-6 was significantly higher in Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs as compared to Htr3a-GFP+ INs negative for tdTOM.
source: Similarly to L1 cells, Car4 expression in L2-6 was significantly higher in Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs as compared to Htr3a-GFP+ INs negative for tdTOM (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A,B, Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3A,B.

claim: All Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs located in L2–6 (7 out of 7) had the characteristic morphology of NGCs.
source: Morphological recovery of Hmx3; tdTOM+/Htr3a-GFP+ INs located in L2–6 revealed that all cells (7 out of 7) had also the characteristic morphology of NGCs (Figure 6—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by morphological reconstruction data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4.

claim: Htr3a-GFP+ INs displaying the molecular, morphological and electrophysiological properties of NGC INs originate from Hmx3-expressing cells in the embryonic POA.

claim: About 60–70% of cortical INs is generated from NKX2.1-expressing progenitors located in the medial ganglionic eminence (MGE).

evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Southwell et al., 2012).
